findings.finding: Missing/null mtime_ticks cast to zero and entered the recoverable dynamic-file mismatch path, contrary to the declared malformed-token contract. Size also lacked a strict integer type check.
findings.resolution: Validate integer size and mtime_ticks before file comparisons; reject nonpositive/out-of-range UTC ticks. All later comparisons use the validated values. The native probe adds missing/null/bool/string/fractional/range cases.

findings.finding: The replay injected the next row from verify_control after the mocked workbook calculation returned, while the document said it happened during calculation. That wording could confuse forced race reproduction with measured calculation latency.
findings.resolution: The document now specifies forced injection after calculation, during pre-edit reverification. It expressly states that the replay does not measure actual Excel COM latency.
findings.verification: Independently compared the corrected document with the inspected replay script and executed the replay.

review_conclusions: ObservationSuspended is a separate ControlUnavailable subtype. Same-run token loss or superseded observations have a connected recovery path; a changed run, parser error, stale same observation and unclassified error still escape that path.
The adapter invalidates cached snapshots on observation suspension and preserves recognition of a new row consumed by a guard read. This avoids treating cached old data as the recovery baseline.

The session resets controller/workbook history and clears stale proposals, reuses the first-valid-baseline/fresh-different-layer barrier, and does not request settings recovery for CSV waits. Readiness loss, cached rows and automatic-image admission do not bypass that barrier in the exercised cases.

Native observation_wait is set only by explicit file-evidence rejection branches. Malformed token validation precedes those branches in the final commit. Unknown I/O errors retain terminal classification.

The durable edit/save marker check precedes exception-type recovery. All tested classified and unclassified errors after either marker become AmbiguousWriteError and latch the fault; no retry or rollback occurs.

Timing messages use elapsed monotonic times in finally blocks for process and apply attempts. Failed calculations and apply waits emit timings. Save request duration is explicitly distinguished from Save success. These logs do not establish a total hard cap or measured COM performance.

The output formulas, step and saturation limits, CSV parser, job anchoring and settings audit were not changed. The version, workflow ZIP names and package source requirements agree. No binary release artifact was changed by this diff.

Process failure and pre-edit wait both emit the appropriate timing logs; apply duration does not claim Save success.

limits: Native Windows/PowerShell guard and UI execution were reviewed statically here. The final ddd92159 Windows candidate run was pending outside this reviewer environment at review completion; no passed result is claimed for it.

Actual Excel COM was not run or timed. The configured ordinary response timeout is 8 seconds and initialization uses max(30 seconds, configured timeout); those are response waits, not a total processing-time measurement or hard cap.
Forced append injection reproduces a race family and does not establish that calculation lasted a whole layer interval in the reported machine run.

The final CSV cannot establish the exact in-flight append/partial-write state or exception time of the original incident. The extension disconnect path is reproduced; the reason BinderJet stopped before 259 is not established.
